summary: Updates RFC 3161 so a time-stamping authority can name its signing certificate using ESSCertIDv2, which allows hash functions other than SHA-1. It is a small proposed-standard change to support stronger hashes.

plainLanguage.summary: This update lets RFC 3161 time-stamp tokens identify the signer's certificate with ESSCertIDv2, which supports hash algorithms other than SHA-1. It changes certificate references in request, response, and verification rules.

subtitle: Allows RFC 3161 time-stamp tokens to identify signer certificates using ESSCertIDv2.

tldr.problem: RFC 3161's ESSCertID certificate identifier supports SHA-1 only.
tldr.mechanism: This document updates three RFC 3161 passages to allow ESSCertIDv2 and SigningCertificateV2 for other hash algorithms.
tldr.outcome: It supports interoperability and migration away from SHA-1 and updates RFC 3161.

today: RFC 5816 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 3161. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The SHA-1 Limitation
sections.content:
RFC 3161 requires the CMS SignedData that signs a time-stamp token to include a signed attribute identifying the signer's certificate. The earlier ESSCertID mechanism allowed only SHA-1 for that identifier.

RFC 5035 introduced ESSCertIDv2 to allow any hash algorithm. This RFC updates RFC 3161 so the newer identifier can be used.
sections.plainLanguage: The earlier certificate identifier was limited to SHA-1. ESSCertIDv2 allows the identifier to use other hash algorithms.

sections.title: Changes to Request and Response Rules
sections.content:
When certReq is true, the TSA must provide the certificate identified by ESSCertID or ESSCertIDv2 in the response certificates field. A time-stamp token may identify the TSA certificate using either identifier.

For algorithms other than SHA-1, SigningCertificateV2 MUST be used and SHOULD NOT be used for SHA-1. For backward compatibility, both identifiers MAY appear, and a system MAY ignore ESSCertIDv2 if it has not implemented RFC 5035.
sections.plainLanguage: The updated rules allow either certificate identifier. Systems use the version-two attribute with a hash algorithm other than SHA-1.

sections.title: Security and Migration
sections.content:
The RFC says the update aims to let implementers comply with policies phasing out SHA-1. Its motivation is interoperability and migration to other hash algorithms, rather than mitigating new security issues.

It incorporates the security considerations of RFC 5035.
sections.plainLanguage: The change makes it possible to use other hash algorithms for the certificate identifier. The RFC describes this as a migration and interoperability update.
